title: Catalog API pagination contract
purpose: Document the two competing catalog API pagination drafts and the resulting unresolved contract so a human can select the authoritative version before implementation.

scope.text: The catalog API has two competing pagination drafts, and the authoritative contract has not been selected.

requirements.text: GET /v1/items returns a JSON object with an items array and next_cursor string.
UI must support moving to the next page.
GET /v1/items returns a top-level JSON array and uses page and page_size query parameters.

stories.text: If a human selects draft A as the authoritative catalog API contract, a UI consumer can request the first items page and then move to the next page using the returned next_cursor.
acceptance_criteria: Given a human has selected draft A as the authoritative contract, when a UI consumer calls GET /v1/items, then the response is a JSON object whose items array contains catalog items and whose next_cursor value is a string.

Given a human has selected draft A as the authoritative contract and the response provides a next_cursor value, when the UI consumer moves to the next page, then the UI requests and presents the subsequent page of catalog items.

stories.text: If a human selects draft B as the authoritative catalog API contract, a UI consumer can request catalog items by page using page and page_size query parameters.
acceptance_criteria: Given a human has selected draft B as the authoritative contract, when a UI consumer calls GET /v1/items with page and page_size query parameters, then the response is a top-level JSON array of catalog items corresponding to the requested page.

dependencies.text: The authoritative catalog API contract has not been selected between draft A and draft B.

risks.text: Implementing draft A's object-with-next_cursor response would not satisfy draft B's top-level array and page/page_size request shape, and implementing draft B would not satisfy draft A's response shape and next_cursor-based paging.

open_questions: Which catalog API draft is authoritative: draft A or draft B?
Who has authority to select the authoritative catalog API contract?
If draft A is selected, how does a client make the subsequent request after receiving a next_cursor value?
If draft B is selected, what are the default and maximum values for page and page_size?
If draft A is selected, does the request carry any pagination parameter, or is the first request issued without one?
